The 2019–20 season was [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]'s 28th season in the [[Premier League]] and their 45th consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]]. The club participated in the [[2019–20 Premier League|Premier League]], finishing third, and reached the semi-finals of the [[2019–20 FA Cup|FA Cup]], the [[2019–20 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]]. The defeat in the Europa League made this United's first hat-trick of trophyless seasons since [[1988–89 Manchester United F.C. season|1989]].

This was United's first full season under manager [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]], who took permanent charge in March 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=Solskjaer announced as full-time manager |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/manchester-united-announces-ole-gunnar-solskjaer-as-full-time-manager |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=28 March 2019 |access-date=29 August 2019 }}</ref> It was also their first season since [[2008–09 Manchester United F.C. season|2008–09]] and [[2013–14 Manchester United F.C. season|2013–14]] without [[Captain (association football)|club captain]] [[Antonio Valencia]] and [[Ander Herrera]], who both left the club at the end of the [[2018–19 Manchester United F.C. season|previous season]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Old Trafford says farewell to Valencia |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/antonio-valencia-says-his-farewells-at-old-trafford-after-10-years |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=12 May 2019 |access-date=14 May 2019 }}</ref> Solskjær named [[Ashley Young]] as Valencia's successor as club captain.<ref>{{cite news |first=Sam |last=Carney |title=Ole says Young will be new club captain |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/solskjaer-indicates-ashley-young-will-be-man-utd-club-captain |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=3 August 2019 |access-date=11 August 2019 }}</ref> Upon Young's departure for [[Inter Milan]] in January 2020, he was replaced as club captain by [[Harry Maguire]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Sam |last=Carney |title=Maguire to be new United captain |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/harry-maguire-confirmed-as-new-man-utd-captain |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=17 January 2020 |access-date=17 January 2020 }}</ref>

After being no higher than fifth place in the league since their sixth match in September 2019, United moved up to third place with a draw at home to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in the penultimate match of the season; they confirmed their third-place finish and a spot in the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League]] with a 2–0 victory at [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] on the final day of the season on 26 July, their 14th consecutive league game without defeat. The season featured a three-month hiatus from March to June 2020 after the outbreak of the global [[COVID-19 pandemic]].

==Pre-season and friendlies==
===Pre-season===
{{See also|2019 International Champions Cup}}

United preceded their 2019–20 campaign with a pre-season tour, with matches in Australia, Singapore, China, Norway and Wales. The first two matches were played at the [[Perth Stadium]] in [[Perth]], Australia; the first was a 2–0 win over local side [[Perth Glory FC|Perth Glory]], with goals from [[Marcus Rashford]] and [[James Garner (footballer, born 2001)|James Garner]],<ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Froggatt |title=Rashford and Garner score as United beat Perth Glory |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/tour-2019-match-report-of-man-utd-v-perth-glory-in-australia |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=13 July 2019 |access-date=20 July 2019 }}</ref> followed by a meeting with [[Leeds United F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|historic rivals]] [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], which the Red Devils won 4–0 thanks to goals from Rashford, [[Phil Jones (footballer, born 1992)|Phil Jones]], [[Anthony Martial]], as well as a maiden senior goal for [[Mason Greenwood]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Froggatt |title=Reds turn on the style to beat rivals Leeds |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-for-man-utd-v-leeds-during-tour-2019-in-australia |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=17 July 2019 |access-date=20 July 2019 }}</ref>

United also took part in the [[2019 International Champions Cup]]. They began with a match against [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] in Singapore on 20 July, in which Greenwood scored the only goal to give United a 1–0 win,<ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Froggatt |title=Greenwood scores again as United beat Inter |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-for-man-united-v-inter-milan-in-singapore-during-tour-2019 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=20 July 2019 |access-date=20 July 2019 }}</ref> followed by a match against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in Shanghai five days later, winning 2–1 thanks to goals from Martial and [[Angel Gomes]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Joe |last=Ganley |title=Reds see off rivals Spurs in Shanghai |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/tottenham-hotspur-v-man-united-match-report-from-shanghai-on-tour-2019 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=25 July 2019 |access-date=25 July 2019 }}</ref> They then travelled to Norway to play an additional friendly against [[Kristiansund BK]], the hometown club of Norwegian manager Ole Gunnar Solskjær, winning it 1–0 through an injury-time penalty by [[Juan Mata]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Mata keeps United's winning run going in Oslo |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/friendly-match-report-kristiansund-v-man-utd-in-oslo |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=30 July 2019 |access-date=30 July 2019 }}</ref> Their final game in the International Champions Cup and final pre-season game saw them play against [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] in Cardiff on 3 August, winning 5–4 in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] after the match ended in a 2–2 draw, with goals from Rashford and [[Jesse Lingard]]; [[Wales national football team|Wales]] international [[Daniel James (footballer)|Daniel James]] scored the winning penalty.<ref>{{cite news |first=Sam |last=Carney |title=Reds spot on to beat AC Milan on penalties |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-for-man-utd-ac-milan-in-cardiff |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=3 August 2019 |access-date=3 August 2019 }}</ref>

===Mid-season===

As a result of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], Premier League football was suspended on 13 March 2020; following the announcement in early June that the league would be resuming in mid-June, United first played an intra-squad friendly match at [[Old Trafford]],<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Bostock |title=United return to Old Trafford for a training game |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-united-return-to-old-trafford-for-a-training-game |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=6 June 2020 |access-date=13 June 2020 }}</ref> before arranging another friendly against [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] for 9 June; however, this match was cancelled after Stoke manager [[Michael O'Neill (footballer)|Michael O'Neill]] tested positive for [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Stoke abort Manchester United friendly after O'Neill tests positive for Covid-19 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/jun/09/stoke-scrap-manchester-united-friendly-after-oneill-tests-positive-for-covid-19 |work=The Guardian |publisher=Guardian News & Media |date=9 June 2020 |access-date=13 June 2020 }}</ref> United did eventually return to action on 12 June, playing two matches against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] behind closed doors at Old Trafford; West Brom won the first match 2–1, but United won the second 3–1.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Reds warm up for restart with West Brom friendlies |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-v-west-brom-friendly-games-at-old-trafford-before-restart |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=12 June 2020 |access-date=13 June 2020 }}</ref>

==Premier League==
{{main|2019–20 Premier League}}

===Matches===
The [[Premier League]] fixtures were announced on 13 June 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=Premier League fixtures for 2019/20 announced |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1240976 |website=premierleague.com |publisher=Premier League |date=16 June 2019 |access-date=30 January 2020 }}</ref> Manchester United began their season at home to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on 11 August; a goal in each half from [[Marcus Rashford]], in addition to goals from [[Anthony Martial]] and debutant [[Daniel James (footballer)|Daniel James]], gave United a 4–0 win.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 4-0 Chelsea: Marcus Rashford stars in fine win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49223795 |work=BBC Sport |date=11 August 2019 |access-date=18 August 2019 }}</ref> United were held to a 1–1 draw by [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] in their next game; Martial opened the scoring with his 50th goal for the club before [[Rúben Neves]] equalised with a long-range strike, only for [[Paul Pogba]] to miss from the penalty spot midway through the second half.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Wolves 1-1 Man Utd: Paul Pogba misses penalty at Molineux |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49315240 |work=BBC Sport |date=19 August 2019 |access-date=24 August 2019 }}</ref> United suffered their first defeat of the season on 24 August, losing 2–1 at home to [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]. After [[Jordan Ayew]] put the Eagles 1–0 up against the run of play with just over half an hour gone, it took until the final minute of normal time for Daniel James to find the equaliser; however, [[Patrick van Aanholt]]'s injury-time strike gave Palace their first league win over United since May 1991 and their first league win at Old Trafford since December 1989.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Crystal Palace shock Man Utd with injury-time winner |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49378901 |work=BBC Sport |date=24 August 2019 |access-date=24 August 2019 }}</ref> James continued his goalscoring form in United's final game before the international break away to [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], opening the scoring after 10 minutes. [[Jannik Vestergaard]] equalised for the home side just before the hour mark, but although [[Kevin Danso]] was sent off with 17 minutes to go, United were unable to make their numerical advantage count and the match finished as a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Southampton 1-1 Man Utd: Jannik Vestergaard header earns 10-man Saints a point |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49456551 |work=BBC Sport |date=31 August 2019 |access-date=18 September 2019 }}</ref>

United returned to action after the international break with a home game against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]. Marcus Rashford scored the only goal of the game from the penalty spot to give United their first win since the opening day of the season.<ref>{{cite news |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez |title=Manchester United 1-0 Leicester City: Marcus Rashford penalty clinches victory |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49617987 |work=BBC Sport |date=14 September 2019 |access-date=18 September 2019 }}</ref> United's next match, away to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]], ended in a 2–0 defeat, with a goal each from [[Andriy Yarmolenko]] and [[Aaron Cresswell]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Matthew |last=Howarth |title=West Ham United 2-0 Manchester United: Hammers too strong for toothless visitors |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49705145 |work=BBC Sport |date=22 September 2019 |access-date=8 November 2019 }}</ref> United then played [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] at home; [[Scott McTominay]] opened the scoring with his first senior goal at Old Trafford, but [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]] was awarded the equaliser after the [[video assistant referee]] (VAR) overruled the [[Assistant referee (association football)|assistant referee]]'s original decision that he was [[Offside (association football)|offside]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Man Utd 1-1 Arsenal: Aubameyang earns Gunners a point |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49791610 |work=BBC Sport |date=30 September 2019 |access-date=8 November 2019 }}</ref> United's final match before the second international break of the season was away to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], who won 1–0 thanks to a goal from [[Matty Longstaff]] on his senior debut.<ref>{{cite news |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez |title=Newcastle 1-0 Man Utd: Matty Longstaff scores winner on debut |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49868087 |work=BBC Sport |date=6 October 2019 |access-date=8 November 2019 }}</ref>

United returned to action after the second international break with a home game against [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|arch-rivals]] [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]. Marcus Rashford opened the scoring after a VAR check, as [[Victor Lindelöf]] was ruled not to have fouled [[Divock Origi]]. The VAR was used again to check a goal scored by [[Sadio Mané]], which appeared to have come off his arm, and was eventually ruled out for [[Fouls and misconduct (association football)|handball]]. Liverpool did manage to find an equaliser through [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] [[Adam Lallana]] in the 85th minute to secure a vital point for both teams. The result meant that United ended Liverpool's winning streak at 18 games.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Man Utd 1-1 Liverpool: Adam Lallana saves Reds' unbeaten start |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50030956 |work=BBC Sport |date=20 October 2019 |access-date=21 October 2019 }}</ref> On 27 October 2019, [[Scott McTominay]] netted United's recordbreaking 2,000th Premier League goal in a 3–1 victory against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] at [[Carrow Road]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Emlyn |last=Begley |title=Man Utd beat Norwich 3-1 to end bad away run in Premier League |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50113574|work=BBC Sport |date=27 October 2019 |access-date=20 December 2019 }}</ref> Rashford had a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] saved by [[Tim Krul]] a few minutes later, but scored on United's next attack to put them 2–0 up with less than half an hour played. United were awarded a second penalty for a handball by [[Todd Cantwell]], but despite a change of taker, Krul was able to make another save from Martial. Like Rashford, Martial made amends later by scoring United's third goal. [[Onel Hernández]] scored a consolation goal for Norwich City in the 88th minute.<ref>{{cite news |first=Emlyn |last=Begley |title=Man Utd beat Norwich 3-1 to end bad away run in Premier League |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50113574 |work=BBC Sport |date=27 October 2019 |access-date=8 November 2019 }}</ref>

To begin November, United made the trip to [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]], where former United striker [[Joshua King (footballer, born 1992)|Joshua King]] scored on the stroke of half-time to give Bournemouth a 1–0 win. The result dropped United down to 10th position in the league table and gave Bournemouth their first win since September 2019.<ref>{{cite news |first=Ben |last=Collins |title=Bournemouth 1-0 Manchester United: Joshua King's goal gives Cherries first win since September |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50191004 |work=BBC Sport |date=2 November 2019 |access-date=2 November 2019 }}</ref> United's next home match before the third international break of the season was against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]], where goals from [[Andreas Pereira]] (his first of the season), Scott McTominay and Marcus Rashford helped United to a 3–1 win.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 3-1 Brighton: United go seventh after comfortable win over Brighton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50278822 |work=BBC Sport |date=10 November 2019 |access-date=11 November 2019 }}</ref> The second goal was initially given as an own goal by [[Davy Pröpper]], but was later awarded to McTominay.<ref>{{cite news |first=Sam |last=Carney |title=McTominay awarded goal in Brighton win |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/scott-mctominay-awarded-second-goal-in-uniteds-3-1-win-over-brighton |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=13 November 2019 |access-date=13 November 2019 }}</ref> United drew against [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]]<ref>{{Cite news |first=Neil |last=Johnston |title=Sheff Utd 3-3 Man Utd: Oliver McBurnie scores dramatic late equaliser |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50449170|work=BBC Sport |date=24 November 2019 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref> in a game which saw [[Brandon Williams (footballer)|Brandon Williams]] scoring his first senior goal and [[Mason Greenwood]] scoring his first Premier League goal, and [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], in which [[Victor Lindelöf]] scored his first goal of the season,<ref>{{Cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Man Utd 2-2 Aston Villa: Red Devils held by resolute Villans |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50534315|work=BBC Sport |date=1 December 2019 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref> On 4 December, United beat [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] 2–1 through a Marcus Rashford brace.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 2-1 Tottenham Hotspur: Marcus Rashford scores twice as Jose Mourinho loses first Spurs game |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50568388|work=BBC Sport |date=4 December 2019 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref> Three days later, they faced last season's champions [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the [[Manchester derby]] at the [[City of Manchester Stadium|Etihad Stadium]]. Twenty minutes into the first half, United were awarded a penalty, which Rashford converted; five minutes later, Anthony Martial made the scoreline 2–0. Despite a goal for City by [[Nicolás Otamendi]] late into the second half, United emerged victorious.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Chris |last=Bevan |title=Manchester City 1-2 Manchester United: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's side dent City's title hopes |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50611309|work=BBC Sport |date=7 December 2019 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref> A draw against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]]<ref>{{Cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Man United 1-1 Everton: Mason Greenwood secures draw for Red Devils at Old Trafford |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50702876|work=BBC Sport |date=15 December 2019 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref> was followed by defeat at [[Watford F.C.|Watford]].<ref>{{Cite news |first=Steve |last=Sutcliffe |title=Watford 2-0 Manchester United: David de Gea error and Troy Deeney penalty lift Hornets' hopes of avoiding relegation |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50797990|work=BBC Sport |date=22 December 2019 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref> Victories against Newcastle United<ref>{{Cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 4-1 Newcastle United: Anthony Martial stars in thumping win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50847256|work=BBC Sport |date=26 December 2019 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref> and [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]]<ref>{{Cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Burnley 0-2 Manchester United: Red Devils up to fifth with victory |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50875692|work=BBC Sport |date=28 December 2019 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref> brought the club's decade to a close.

The 2020s was started with a defeat at Arsenal on New Year's Day.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Alistair |last=Magowan|title=Arsenal 2-0 Man Utd: Gunners secure first win under Mikel Arteta |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50908732|work=BBC Sport |date=1 January 2020 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref> Ten days later, United recorded their first win of the decade with a 4–0 demolition of Norwich City; Rashford scored twice, Martial and Greenwood scored once each.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez|title=Manchester United 4-0 Norwich City: Marcus Rashford scores twice on 200th appearance |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50990602|work=BBC Sport |date=11 January 2020 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref> On the following three league matches the club failed to score, the first two ended in 2–0 defeats; matches against the runaway league leaders Liverpool<ref>{{Cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty|title=Liverpool 2-0 Manchester United: Virgil van Dijk and Mohamed Salah goals secure win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51080695|work=BBC Sport |date=19 January 2020 |access-date=11 March 2020 }}</ref> and a revenge by Burnley, which turned out to be their last defeat of the season,<ref>{{Cite news |first=Callum |last=Matthews|title=Manchester United 0-2 Burnley: Clarets shock United at Old Trafford |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51115604|work=BBC Sport |date=22 January 2020 |access-date=11 March 2020 }}</ref> were followed by a goalless draw against Wolverhampton Wanderers.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone|title=Manchester United 0-0 Wolverhampton Wanderers |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51246502|work=BBC Sport |date=1 February 2020 |access-date=11 March 2020 }}</ref> After the newly introduced winter break, United got full 3 points at Chelsea, extending their undefeated run against the West London club to six matches.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty|title=Chelsea 0-2 Man Utd: Martial and Maguire score for visitors |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51439302|work=BBC Sport |date=1 February 2020 |access-date=11 March 2020 }}</ref><ref name="MUNCHE"/> Watford was the next victim, falling three goals to nil at Old Trafford.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone|title=Manchester United 3-0 Watford: Fernandes scores first goal as Utd go fifth |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51519244 |work=BBC Sport |date=23 February 2020 |access-date=11 March 2020 }}</ref> The newly recruited Portuguese midfielder [[Bruno Fernandes]] scored the first goal from the spot, his first goal for the club. The fixture against Everton was again ended in a 1–1 draw with [[David de Gea]] making an error leading up to the home side's goal before Fernandes' equaliser, his first open play goal for United.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Alistair |last=Magowan|title=Everton 1-1 Manchester United: Toffees see late goal disallowed |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51601978|work=BBC Sport |date=1 March 2020 |access-date=11 March 2020 }}</ref> The next week, United won 2–0 against Manchester City thanks to a goal by Anthony Martial and a last minute 40-yard volley from Scott McTominay, both of which were the result of goalkeeping errors from City keeper [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]]. The victory completed their first league double over their city rivals since the [[2009–10 Premier League|2009–10 season]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Man Utd 2-0 Man City: Anthony Martial and Scott McTominay score in derby win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51693762 |work=BBC Sport |date=8 March 2020 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref>

Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]], Premier League matches were suspended on 13 March, initially only until 3 April 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Coronavirus: Premier League and EFL suspended in England - Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland halt games |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51867989 |work=BBC Sport |date=13 March 2020 |access-date=29 May 2020 }}</ref> The suspension was made indefinite on 5 April 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Premier League statement on impact of COVID-19 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1651836 |website=premierleague.com |publisher=Premier League |date=5 April 2020 |access-date=23 April 2020 }}</ref> On 28 May, it was announced that the Premier League would return behind closed doors on 17 June.<ref>{{cite web |title=Statement on provisional season restart date |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1674011 |website=premierleague.com |publisher=Premier League |date=28 May 2020 |access-date=29 May 2020 }}</ref>

The return of the league on 19 June saw United draw 1–1 at Tottenham Hotspur; Fernandes equalised with a penalty kick after [[Steven Bergwijn]]'s opening goal.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Tottenham Hotspur 1-1 Manchester United: Bruno Fernandes' late penalty earns visitors draw|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51787532 |work=BBC Sport |date=19 June 2020 |access-date=24 June 2020 }}</ref> In a 3–0 home win against Sheffield United on 24 June, Martial scored his first senior hat-trick, as well as United's first league hat-trick since [[Robin van Persie]] did so on 22 April 2013.<ref>{{cite news|first=Simon|last=Stone|title=Manchester United 3-0 Sheffield United: Anthony Martial hat-trick sinks Blades |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51893551 |work=BBC Sport |date=24 June 2020 |access-date=24 June 2020 }}</ref> On 30 June, after the opening goal by Greenwood, Fernandes scored his first brace for United in a 3–0 win against Brighton & Hove Albion.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez |title=Brighton 0-3 Man Utd: Visitors score through Greenwood and Fernandes' double |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52072990 |work=BBC Sport |date=30 June 2020 |access-date=30 June 2020 }}</ref> Both players found the net again in the match against Bournemouth; Fernandes scored one after Greenwood made his first league brace. Martial and Rashford scored one each as United won 5–2.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 5-2 Bournemouth: Mason Greenwood scores twice in crushing win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52162234|work=BBC Sport |date=4 July 2020 |access-date=4 July 2020 }}</ref> On 9 July, both Fernandes and Greenwood scored again, with [[Paul Pogba]] adding his first goal of the season in a 3–0 win at Aston Villa. The win made United the first team in Premier League history to win four consecutive games by three goals or more, and the first to do so in the top flight since Liverpool in [[1987–88 Football League|October 1987]].<ref>{{Cite news |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez |title=Aston Villa 0-3 Man Utd: Bruno Fernandes, Mason Greenwood and Paul Pogba score |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53283296|work=BBC Sport |date=9 July 2020 |access-date=9 July 2020 }}</ref> United went behind early in their match against Southampton on 13 July, before Rashford and Martial put them into the lead with two quick goals midway through the first half; however, [[Michael Obafemi]] scored a 96th-minute equaliser and the match finished 2–2, denying United an opportunity to jump to third in the table.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Emma |last=Sanders |title=Manchester United 2-2 Southampton: Late equaliser sets back hosts' top-four hopes |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53303199 |work=BBC Sport |date=13 July 2020 |access-date=13 July 2020 }}</ref> Away to Crystal Palace, Rashford scored and then assisted Martial's goal as United won 2–0 at [[Selhurst Park]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Crystal Palace 0-2 Manchester United: Marcus Rashford and Anthony Martial score |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53343861|access-date=16 July 2020 |work=BBC Sport |date=16 July 2020}}</ref> In this match, defender [[Timothy Fosu-Mensah]] made his first start since May 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Tyrone |last=Marshall |title=Why Timothy Fosu-Mensah is starting for Manchester United vs Crystal Palace |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/man-utd-timothy-fosu-mensah-18611270 |work=Manchester Evening News |date=16 July 2020 |access-date=16 July 2020}}</ref> In the penultimate match of the season against West Ham, United went 1–0 down to a [[Michail Antonio]] penalty on the stroke of half-time, but Mason Greenwood's equaliser early in the second half salvaged a 1–1 draw that moved United back into the top four for the first time since September 2019.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 1-1 West Ham: Red Devils need point to reach Champions League place |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53412783 |work=BBC Sport |date=22 July 2020 |access-date=26 July 2020 }}</ref> A third-place finish was confirmed on the final day of the season, as a penalty from Bruno Fernandes – the 14th United had been awarded in the league that season (a Premier League record)<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester United break Premier League penalty record on final day |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/manchester-united/story/4147645/manchester-united-break-premier-league-penalty-record-on-final-day |website=ESPN.co.uk |publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures |date=26 July 2020 |access-date=26 July 2020 }}</ref> – and a 98th-minute goal from [[Jesse Lingard]] – his first in the league since 22 December 2018 – secured a 2–0 victory away to Leicester City, meaning United finished the season unbeaten in their final 14 matches and qualified for the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Leicester City 0-2 Manchester United: Visitors secure Champions League place |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53460592 |work=BBC Sport |date=26 July 2020 |access-date=26 July 2020 }}</ref>

==FA Cup==
As a Premier League side, Manchester United entered the [[2019–20 FA Cup]] in the Third Round Proper. The draw gave United an away tie at fellow Premier League side [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]]. The match was played on 4 January 2020 and finished goalless, requiring a replay later that month.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Wolverhampton Wanderers 0-0 Manchester United, FA Cup third round |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50976111 |work=BBC Sport |date=4 January 2020 |access-date=16 January 2020 }}</ref> The Fourth Round draw took place on 5 January, with United – were they to beat Wolves in their replay – drawn away to either [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] or [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=FA Cup draw: Liverpool, Chelsea and Leicester get away ties in fourth round |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51014668 |work=BBC Sport |date=15 January 2020 |access-date=16 January 2020 }}</ref> The replay was played on 15 January and saw Juan Mata score the only goal of the game to put United through.<ref>{{cite news |first=Gary |last=Rose |title=Manchester United 1-0 Wolverhampton Wanderers, FA Cup third-round replay |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51093972 |work=BBC Sport |date=15 January 2020 |access-date=16 January 2020 }}</ref> Playing at [[Prenton Park]] against Tranmere, who had eliminated Watford just three days prior, United won 6–0; Harry Maguire and [[Diogo Dalot]] both scored their first goals for the club.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Tranmere 0-6 Manchester United: Reds' fans voice anger during FA Cup win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51208521 |work=BBC Sport |date=26 January 2020|access-date=1 February 2020}}</ref> In the fifth round, United came up against [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] and former striker [[Wayne Rooney]]. In a 3–0 win at [[Pride Park Stadium|Pride Park]], [[Odion Ighalo]] scored his first brace for United following [[Luke Shaw]]'s first goal of the season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51726490|title=Derby County 0-3 Manchester United: No joy for Wayne Rooney as Odion Ighalo scores twice|first=Tom|last=Rostance|date=5 March 2020|work=BBC Sport|access-date=6 March 2020}}</ref>

After a three-month delay due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]], the quarter-final tie against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] was played on 27 June 2020. Ighalo opened the scoring before an equaliser from [[Todd Cantwell]]. Deep into extra time, Maguire scored to send United to the semi-finals,<ref>{{Cite news |first=Saj |last=Chowdhury |title=Norwich City 1-2 Manchester United: Harry Maguire scores extra-time winner |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53015159 |work=BBC Sport |date=27 June 2020 |access-date=27 June 2020 }}</ref> where they were drawn against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Having played against Chelsea in the EFL Cup earlier in the season, it was the first time in seven years that United had faced the same opponents in both domestic cup competitions in one season; the last time was also against Chelsea in 2012–13.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Manchester United's duplicate cup draws |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/times-man-utd-played-same-team-in-one-fa-cup-and-league-cup-season |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=1 July 2020 |access-date=10 July 2020 }}</ref> However, the FA Cup results on both occasions were same; United succumbed to Chelsea. They suffered their first defeat to the West London club since the [[2018 FA Cup Final]], as well as ending their 19-game unbeaten run in all competitions.<ref name="MUNCHE">{{Cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty|title=Manchester United 1-3 Chelsea: De Gea errors help settle FA Cup semi-final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53420073|work=BBC Sport |date=19 July 2020 |access-date=19 July 2020 }}</ref>

==EFL Cup==
As one of the seven English sides competing in UEFA competitions in 2019–20, Manchester United entered the [[2019–20 EFL Cup]] in the third round. The draw for the third round took place on 28 August 2019, and saw United given a home tie against [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]]. It was only the second time they had met in a competitive, first-team match; their only other meeting was in the third round of the [[1985–86 FA Cup]], when Manchester United won 2–0.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=United handed home draw in Carabao Cup |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-carabao-cup-third-round-draw-opponents-revealed |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=28 August 2019 |access-date=29 August 2019 }}</ref> The match was played on 25 September, with [[Mason Greenwood]] opening the scoring in the 68th minute; however, 16-year-old [[Luke Matheson (footballer)|Luke Matheson]] equalised for Rochdale eight minutes later. The match finished at 1–1 after 90 minutes and went straight to penalties; [[Sergio Romero]] saved Rochdale's second penalty from [[Jimmy Keohane]], while all Manchester United's kicks were successful, culminating with Daniel James scoring the winning penalty.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Man Utd 1-1 Rochdale (5-3 on pens): United survive scare |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49736850 |website=BBC Sport |date=25 September 2019 |access-date=27 September 2019 }}</ref>

In the fourth round, Manchester United were drawn away to Chelsea; it was the sixth time they had met in the competition, most recently in [[2012–13 Manchester United F.C. season|2012–13]], when Chelsea won 5–4 after extra time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Michael |last=Plant |title=Confirmed: Our Carabao Cup fourth-round opponents |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-discover-carabao-cup-fourth-round-opponents |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=25 September 2019 |access-date=27 September 2019 }}</ref> [[Marcus Rashford]] scored twice to record a 2–1 win,<ref>{{cite news |first=Emlyn |last=Begley|title=Chelsea 1-2 Manchester United: Marcus Rashford puts United into EFL Cup last eight |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50148249 |website=BBC Sport |date=30 October 2019 |access-date=19 December 2019 }}</ref> securing their passage to the fifth round and extending their unbeaten run against Chelsea in all competitions to five matches; their last loss to Chelsea was in the [[2018 FA Cup Final]].<ref name="MUNCHE"/>

United won their fifth round match against the last surviving non-Premier League club, [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]], with goals from Marcus Rashford, [[Anthony Martial]], and an own goal.<ref>{{cite news |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez |title=Manchester United 3-0 Colchester United: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's side reach semi-finals |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50738364 |website=BBC Sport |date=18 December 2019 |access-date=19 December 2019 }}</ref> They were drawn to play [[Manchester derby|local rivals]] [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the two-legged semi-final in January.<ref>{{cite news |first=Jamie |last=Jackson |title=Marcus Rashford downs Colchester once Manchester United find their range |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/dec/18/manchester-united-colchester-carabao-cup-quarter-final-match-report |work=The Guardian |date=18 December 2019 |access-date=19 December 2019 }}</ref> City's 3–1 win in the first leg at Old Trafford was enough to send them to their third successive EFL Cup final,<ref>{{cite news |first=Chris |last=Bevan |title=Carabao Cup - Man Utd 1-3 Man City: Holders overwhelm rivals in semi-final first leg |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50953053 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 January 2020 |access-date=30 January 2020 }}</ref> as United were only able to manage a 1–0 win in the second leg at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Chris |last=Bevan |title=Manchester City 0-1 Manchester United (agg: 3-2): Blues into EFL Cup final despite defeat |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51201817 |website=BBC Sport |date=29 January 2020 |access-date=30 January 2020 }}</ref>

==UEFA Europa League==
===Group stage===
Having finished sixth in the [[2018–19 Premier League]], Manchester United entered the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League]] in the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League group stage|group stage]]. It was the club's first Europa League campaign since winning the competition in [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League|2016–17]], and their fourth in nine years, having also played in the knockout phase in [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League|2011–12]] and [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League|2015–16]]. The draw for the group stage took place in Monaco on 30 August 2019; United were drawn into Group L with Kazakhstani side [[FC Astana|Astana]], Serbian club [[FK Partizan|Partizan]], and [[AZ Alkmaar|AZ]] of the Netherlands. Astana were United's – and any English club's – first ever Kazakhstani opponents, and it would also be the first time they had played against AZ; their only previous meeting with Partizan came in the semi-finals of the [[1965–66 European Cup]], losing 2–0 in Belgrade before a 1–0 win at Old Trafford a week later.<ref>{{cite news |first=Michael |last=Plant |title=United discover Europa League opponents |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-learn-europa-league-group-stage-opponents |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=30 August 2019 |access-date=30 August 2019 }}</ref>

United began their Europa League campaign with a 1–0 win over Astana at Old Trafford on 19 September; [[Mason Greenwood]] scored the only goal of the game, the first of his professional career, cutting inside off the right wing to shoot through the legs of goalkeeper [[Nenad Erić]] and become Manchester United's youngest goalscorer in European football.<ref>{{cite news |first=Neil |last=Johnston |title=Man Utd 1-0 Astana: Mason Greenwood scores first senior goal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49744755 |website=BBC Sport |date=19 September 2019 |access-date=20 September 2019 }}</ref> United's second match, a goalless draw away to AZ, was played at [[Cars Jeans Stadion]] in [[The Hague]] as the roof had collapsed at AZ's [[AFAS Stadion]].<ref>{{cite news |title=AZ Alkmaar: Roof collapses at Eredivisie club's stadium amid high winds |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49309286 |website=BBC Sport |date=10 August 2019 |access-date=30 September 2019 }}</ref> They then made the trip to Belgrade on 24 October, and came away with a 1–0 win thanks to an Anthony Martial penalty.<ref>{{cite news |first=Steve |last=Sutcliffe |title=Partizan Belgrade 0-1 Man Utd: Anthony Martial penalty ends winless away run |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50119152 |website=BBC Sport |date=24 October 2019 |access-date=8 November 2019 }}</ref>

Martial was on the scoresheet again in the reverse fixture at Old Trafford on 7 November, his goal coming between efforts from Greenwood and Rashford. The 3–0 win meant United could no longer be caught by third-placed Partizan in the group standings, confirming their qualification for the knockout phase.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 3-0 Partizan Belgrade: Hosts qualify for Europa League last 32 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50322325 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 November 2019 |access-date=8 November 2019 }}</ref> United fielded a team with an average age of 22 years and 26 days in a 2–1 away defeat to the already-eliminated Astana. The match saw three debutants starting and another three coming on as substitutes.<ref>{{cite news |first=Gemma |last=Thompson |title=FC Astana 2 Manchester United 1 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-astana-v-man-united-europa-league-28-november-2019 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=28 November 2019 |access-date=17 December 2019 }}</ref> [[Jesse Lingard]] captained the side for the first time in his career and scored the opening goal – his first of the season – in the 10th minute; however, a goal from [[Dmitri Shomko]] and an own goal by [[Di'Shon Bernard]] gave Astana the win.<ref>{{cite news |first=Saj |last=Chowdhury |title=Astana 2-1 Manchester United: Solskjaer says youngsters 'knocking on door' of first team |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50508966|website=BBC Sport |date=28 November 2019 |access-date=16 December 2019 }}</ref> United sealed top spot in the group with a 4–0 victory at home to the already-qualified AZ. Greenwood scored the second and fourth goals, and the others were scored by [[Ashley Young]] and [[Juan Mata]], who each scored their first goals of the season; it was Young's first European goal since February 2012, which was scored in the Europa League against another Dutch side, [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]]. It was also United's biggest European victory since the 4–0 Europa League win against yet another Dutch club [[Feyenoord]] in November 2016, when they went on to win the tournament.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Man Utd 4-0 AZ Alkmaar: Mason Greenwood double in emphatic Europa League victory |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50749720 |website=BBC Sport |date=12 December 2019 |access-date=16 December 2019 }}</ref>

===Knockout phase===
Having qualified for the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League knockout phase|knockout phase]] as group winners, Manchester United were seeded for the round of 32 draw and paired with Belgian side [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]], who had dropped down from the Champions League; it was their first meeting since the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League qualifying phase and play-off round#Play-off round|2015–16 UEFA Champions League play-offs]], when Manchester United won 7–1 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=United discover next European opponents |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-discover-europa-league-round-of-32-opponents|website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=16 December 2019 |access-date=16 December 2019 }}</ref> After a 1–1 draw at [[Jan Breydel Stadium]] that saw [[Anthony Martial]] cancel out [[Emmanuel Dennis]]'s opener,<ref>{{cite news |title=Club Bruges 1-1 Manchester United: We were sloppy, says United boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51533294|work=BBC Sport |date=20 February 2020 |access-date=21 February 2020 }}</ref> United won the return leg 5–0 to win 6–1 on aggregate; [[Odion Ighalo]] scored his first goal for the club, [[Fred (footballer, born 1993)|Fred]] scored his first goals of the season, and [[Scott McTominay]] scored his first European goal.<ref>{{cite news |first=Emlyn |last=Begley |title=Manchester United 5-0 Club Bruges: Odion Ighalo scores first goal as hosts progress |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51623256 |work=BBC Sport |date=27 February 2020 |access-date=28 February 2020 }}</ref> The round of 16 draw took place on 28 February, with United paired with Austrian club [[LASK]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Michael |last=Plant |title=Reds discover Europa League last-16 opponents |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-discover-last-16-europa-league-opponents-after-uefa-draw |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=28 February 2020 |access-date=9 March 2020 }}</ref> United won the first leg 5–0.<ref>{{cite news |first=Steve|last=Sutcliffe|title=LASK 0-5 Manchester United: Stunning Odion Ighalo effort sets up Europa League win|work=BBC Sport|date=12 March 2020 |access-date=10 July 2020|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51844660 }}</ref> Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the second leg was played nearly five months later, on 5 August; United went 1–0 down early in the second half, but Jesse Lingard equalised shortly afterwards, before Anthony Martial secured a 2–1 win with three minutes left. That gave United a 7–1 win on aggregate and a place in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news|first=Simon|last=Stone |title=Manchester United 2-1 LASK: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's side complete emphatic win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51844660|work=BBC Sport |date=5 August 2020 |access-date=5 August 2020 }}</ref>

As a further result of the pandemic, the quarter-finals, semi-finals and final of the competition were moved to four venues in the German state of [[North Rhine-Westphalia]], with all matches to be played behind closed doors. The draw for the entire final stage was also performed at the same time on 10 July.<ref>{{cite news |title=Europa League to resume on 5 August, final on 21 August |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/025e-0f9a414021a7-00e4ef531ed6-1000--europa-league-final-eight-in-germany/ |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=17 June 2020 }}</ref> The draw paired Manchester United with Danish side [[F.C. Copenhagen|Copenhagen]] in the quarter-finals, and the match was goalless through the initial 90 minutes, before ultimately being decided by a Bruno Fernandes penalty five minutes into extra time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Tom |last=Rostance |title=Manchester United: Bruno Fernandes penalty books Europa League semi-final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53709142 |work=BBC Sport |date=10 August 2020 |access-date=10 August 2020 }}</ref> In the semi-finals, they would play against the winners of the match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], played the next day; Sevilla also won 1–0, setting up the semi-final to be played in Cologne on 16 August.<ref>{{cite news |first=Emlyn |last=Begley |title=Wolverhampton Wanderers 0-1 Sevilla: Spanish side set up Man Utd semi-final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53727188 |work=BBC Sport |date=11 August 2020 |access-date=13 August 2020 }}</ref> United lost 2–1 despite taking the lead through a Bruno Fernandes penalty in the ninth minute.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Sevilla 2-1 Manchester United: Spanish side come back to reach Europa League final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53793942 |work=BBC Sport |date=16 August 2020 |access-date=16 August 2020 }}</ref>
